comments.body: ⚠️ Bug: Common pronouns resolve any request to the task and skip guards The `pronoun` selector matches very common German words like `es`, `sie`, `diese` and `damit`. When a reference is focused (the seed sets `selectedReferenceId`), `select()` returns `refs[focused]` for any request that contains one of them. For example, "Wie spät ist es?" resolves to `beta`. That has two effects: - A `Resolved` plan is stored, so `render` adds the ARBEITSKONTEXT block to the prompt for unrelated questions. The `unrelatedRequestDoesNotLeakTaskIntoPrompt` test only passes because "Wie warm ist Wien?" contains no pronoun. - In `inspectRequest`, `Resolved` returns `null` before the later checks run. "Merke dir diese Entscheidung" matches `diese`, resolves, and never reaches the `MEMORY_LITERAL_REQUIRED` directive. Turning on the research flag therefore switches off an existing safety directive. Fix: only let a bare pronoun resolve when the request also names the task scope or a reference (`scopeCue`, or a mention). Also run the memory-literal and correction checks before the working-task block. Add tests for "Wie spät ist es?" and "Merke dir diese Entscheidung". **Require a scope cue or explicit mention before a bare pronoun can select the focused reference:** ```` val relative = other.containsMatchIn(raw) || previous.containsMatchIn(raw) || ordinal.containsMatchIn(raw) val pronounOnly = pronoun.containsMatchIn(raw) && scopeCue.containsMatchIn(raw) val hasSelector = relative || pronounOnly if (mentions.isEmpty() && !hasSelector && !scopeCue.containsMatchIn(raw)) return WorkingTaskDecision.NoMatch ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? ⚠️ Bug: Prefix allowlist makes 'Aber Bernstein nicht.' resolve to the rejected ref In this commit, a trailing `nicht` only counts as a rejection when the words before the label are empty or appear in a short allowlist (`rejectsNamed`, L175-181). Before, `X nicht` was rejected wherever it appeared. Now a short rejection with any other lead word passes as a selection. Take "Aber Bernstein nicht.", "Also Bernstein nicht.", "Lieber Bernstein nicht." or "Okay, Bernstein nicht.": the prefix is `[aber]`, `[also]`, etc., so `rejectingLead` is false. None of the `rejectsReference` regexes match either, since they need a following selector, an ordinal, `meine`, or a leading `nicht`. `select` then returns the explicitly named reference, and `resolve` returns `Resolved` with the target the owner just rejected. That is the exact failure that led to REJECT_PROMOTION. The allowlist only exists to keep questions like "Läuft Bernstein nicht?" from counting as rejections. A safer approach is to go back to treating `tail == [nicht]` as a rejection by default, and exempt only interrogative or predicate forms (a verb before the label, or a trailing `?`). Ambiguous phrasings should then return Clarify instead of resolving. **Fail closed: treat a bare trailing 'nicht' as a rejection unless the utterance is a question or a verb comes before the label:** ```` val isQuestion = input.trimEnd().endsWith("?") val predicateLead = prefix.isNotEmpty() && prefix.first() in setOf("wieso", "warum", "weshalb", "läuft", "funktioniert", "geht") val rejectingLead = !isQuestion && !predicateLead before >= 0 && inputWords[before] in setOf("nicht", "kein", "keine", "keinen") || rejectingLead && tail == listOf("nicht") || tail == listOf("ist", "es", "nicht") ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful?
